Foi, ao longo de toda a história recente, a presença policial nas grandes cidades — sobretudo Lisboa e Porto — ao contrário da GNR, que cobria o interior, as estradas e o litoral. Essa distinção não é apenas geográfica: é uma distinção de ritmo, de perfil e de pressão. Uma polícia de cidade vive o chão de rua, freguesia a freguesia, o trânsito, o mercado, a proximidade e o barulho de quem está sempre à porta. Durante o Estado Novo, a PSP, como todas as forças de segurança, funcionou dentro de uma ordem política autoritária. É uma parte da história que não se pode apagar nem glorificar demais: a instituição serviu o regime da mesma maneira que serviria a República depois, porque é uma instituição estrutural, não uma ideologia. Distinguir isso não é pedantismo; é o primeiro exercício de leitura honesta de qualquer dossiê sobre polícia. O dragão da GNR escreveu sobre essa linha antes, com um tom que não esconde a tensão: GNR — O Dragão que Guarda a Lei . 1832 A Guarda Nacional surge Nasce com a necessidade de organizar a segurança nas cidades e nos espaços de conflito do século XIX. O nome e a estrutura vão mudando, mas a função urbana deixa marcas. 1900s–1930s A PSP consolida-se A polícia de Lisboa e Porto ganha maior capacidade de intervenção urbana, com unidades que antes eram mais dispersas a tornarem-se instituições de presença constante. 1933–1974 Estado Novo A PSP funciona no quadro de uma ditadura. Não é só "força de ordem" — é uma instituição envolvida na vida política, com o dever de obediência e a margem que toda a polícia tem. Um dossiê honesto não esconde essa linha; ela é o pano de fundo das perguntas sobre coragem e sobre obediência. 1974 em diante A democracia republicana Após o 25 de Abril, a PSP passa a fazer parte de uma ordem democrática com novas regras, novas expectativas e novas tensões entre obediência, lei e intervenção. Uma das perguntas que atravessa o dossiê não é apenas histórica. É ética. Se a polícia acata ordens, até quando acata? Se acata sempre, até que ponto foi "força pública" em vez de "braço do poder"? O blog já escreveu sobre essa questão com outra inclinação, num tom que mistura sistema, ética e ironia: Discurso do Eterno Macaco às Forças de Segurança do Mundo . A leitura completa ajuda a entender que a PSP nunca é só um braço; às vezes é o reflexo de um país inteiro. 02 · SÍMBOLOS O Tigre: três línguas, um animal O Tigre da PSP não é um acidente gráfico. É um animal que carrega coragem, força e presença; é também um símbolo que, em Portugal e na Ásia, fala línguas muito diferentes. Por isso é normal que o mesmo símbolo soe diferente dependendo de quem o olha e de onde o olha. Daqui nasce uma das lições centrais deste artigo: o símbolo não é uma tradução, é um convite para ler o contexto. Em Portugal, o tigre evoca a proeza, a vigília, a rapidez, a força necessária para a rua e para a crise. Isso não significa que seja "o animal do mal" ou "o animal da barbárie"; é um animal que, no imaginário público, tende a oscilar entre força necessária e força excessiva. Nesta página, trabalhamos essa dualidade de forma intencional: o tigre como coragem, não como crueldade, e reconhecendo que a crueldade existe e que a coragem, quando se desvia da sua função, pode tornar-se violência. Na Ásia, o tigre carrega um peso muito mais antigo e muito mais aberto. É um dos animais mais importantes da cultura chinesa, coreana, japonesa e vietnamita. Não é o dragão, que é celestial e raramente visto de perto. É o tigre: terrestre, audacioso, protetor em muitos contextos, símbolo de homens corajosos em outros, presença de bravura em gestos que exigem coragem e não apenas força. Quando se diz que o tigre é símbolo dos homens corajosos na Ásia, não é uma frase decorativa; é uma observação de que a coragem, na Ásia, está ligada ao animal que enfrenta, protege, avança e, em muitas lendas, não recua. 03 · ÁSIA Na Ásia, o tigre dos homens corajosos A afirmação de que "na Ásia também o Tigre é símbolo dos homens corajosos" é mais profunda do que parece. Na cartografia cultural asiática o tigre é, frequentemente, o animal que liga o homem à sua coragem de forma mais direta do que o dragão. O dragão é, em grande parte da Ásia, o poder celestial, a sabedoria, a água e a chuva, o que unifica e o que governa. O tigre é o corpo que age. É o animal que corre, que protege o território, que enfrenta o perigo, que não representa apenas o poder do céu, mas a coragem de quem está em terra firme. Na China, o tigre é um dos quatro animais sagrados, ao lado do dragão azul, da ave vermelha (fénix) e da tartaruga negra. O tigre azul (青虎) pode aparecer em muitas variantes; em algumas tradições é protetor, noutras é o animal que combate a energia negativa. Há um detalhe surpreendente na leitura ocidental comum: o tigre asiático não é apenas "o animal feroz". É a força que o homem cultiva para estar à frente do perigo sem se deixar levar por ele. Essa é a coragem que interessa a este artigo: não a força que ataca, mas a coragem que enfrenta com responsabilidade. No Japão, o tigre aparece em mitologia, em trajes de teatro e em armaduras, como símbolo de proteção e bravura. Na Coreia, o tigre é, junto com o dragão, um dos dois animais que aparecem tanto na imagética protetora como na lenda. No Vietname, o tigre é fortemente associado à resistência e à coragem nacional. Em todas essas culturas, há uma linha comum: o tigre é usado para falar de homens que a exercem, não apenas de animais que fazem medo. Não é estranho, portanto, que uma polícia portuguesa use um tigre no seu emblema. O que é estranho — ou pelo menos controverso — é usar um símbolo associado à coragem e depois esquecer que a coragem exige limites. A diferença entre coragem e brutalidade é de intenção, de proporcionalidade, de cuidado com o inocente. Essa distinção é o trabalho central não só de um dossiê, mas de uma democracia que quer olhar para a sua polícia sem desviar os olhos nem usar a retórica para fechar os olhos. Comentário pedagógico — o símbolo como convite à introspecção O tigre da PSP não deve ser apenas uma imagem de força. Deve ser um lembrete de que a coragem de um homem está envolvida na coragem de um animal — a de avançar quando é necessário, a de recuar quando a lei e a dignidade exigem. Quando um símbolo de coragem é usado sem reflexão, corre-se o risco de transformar coragem em licença para hiper-reacção. Por isso, ler símbolos de força pública exige mais que admiração: exige a pergunta sobre os limites. Para aprofundar essa leitura, o blog deu já outros passos: Police Groups in Society — A Technical Manual , Police the Police e Human Rights Include You . A estrutura é uma das coisas que mais muda e mais se confunde; não é raro que o cidadão comum misture PSP, GNR, PJ e outras forças num só bloco. Para ler a PSP é preciso ler, antes de tudo, a sua função básica: garantir a segurança pública nas zonas urbanas, prestar serviço de proximidade, fazer cumprir a lei, entrar em contextos de conflito, proteger pessoas e empresas e, em muitos casos, ser a face mais visível do Estado no dia a dia. It lives in a terminal, in a repository with a README, behind one command that installs it. This manual is about that command: how to build a virtual environment, how to keep it out of the system, and thirty real GitHub projects worth the trouble — from posting to Mastodon to OCR on a scanned contract. Nineteen parts Thirty apps venv · pipx · uv Install builder Ten errors, solved Every repo linked I have never made a venv Part 02: seven commands, one afternoon, and nothing else on your machine changes. Show me the tools first Part 06: every tool with its package, version, home page and one-line purpose, plus the command for your machine. Just give me the command Part 03: one isolated environment per app, and no dependency conflicts. An install just failed Part 16: the ten messages that stop people, and the fix for each one. 01 Never install into the system Python Almost every broken Python install starts with one of two sentences: "it worked on my machine" and "I ran it with sudo". Both are the same mistake — installing a project's dependencies into the one interpreter your operating system uses to run itself. There is a rule that removes the whole class of problem, and it fits in three lines. One: the system Python belongs to the system Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, macOS and Arch all ship Python because parts of the operating system are written in it. Installing packages into it means two projects can demand two versions of the same library, and the loser is usually your desktop. Modern distributions now refuse: pip exits with error: externally-managed-environment , which is not a bug, it is a locked door with a reason. Two: a project gets a venv, an app gets pipx If you will import the thing from your own code, it belongs in a virtual environment inside the project folder. If you will only type its name at the prompt, it belongs in pipx (or uv), which gives the app its own private venv and puts a single launcher on your PATH. Nothing else on the machine sees it. Three: no sudo, ever, for pip The single exception is your distribution's package manager — apt install python3-venv , dnf install python3-pip — which installs the tooling, never a project's dependencies. If a README tells you to sudo pip install , the README is old; use the project's pyproject or the PyPI name with pipx. What that error actually says PEP 668 lets a distribution mark its interpreter as externally managed, with an EXTERNALLY-MANAGED marker file next to the standard library. pip reads it and stops. You can override it with --break-system-packages ; you should not, and no command in this manual needs it. The escape hatch is a venv, which is one command away. Three tools, three jobs Tool What it is for Use it when What it costs venv A folder with its own Python, its own pip and its own site-packages. Built into Python since 3.3. You are writing code that imports the library, or you need an exact pinned set of versions for one project. 20–200 MB per environment, and one activation command per terminal. pipx A manager of isolated environments, one per command-line app, with a launcher symlinked into ~/.local/bin . The package provides a command you run (yt-dlp, toot, csvkit) and you never import it. A few MB per app; the disk cost is the price of never having a dependency conflict again. uv A single fast binary that does venvs, pip installs, Python version downloads and tool installs — the same jobs, in seconds. You install tools often, or you are tired of waiting for a resolver. uvx also runs an app without installing it at all. One more binary to trust and to update; it is written in Rust, not Python. The whole idea, on one screen One environment per app, no activation needed, and the command is addressed by its full path. This is the pattern the rest of the manual refines; everything else is convenience built on top of it. python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/media ~/.venvs/media/bin/pip install --upgrade pip ~/.venvs/media/bin/pip install yt-dlp ~/.venvs/media/bin/yt-dlp --version Nothing was installed system-wide, nothing needs sudo, and deleting ~/.venvs/media removes every trace. The three drawbacks are that the path is long, that each app needs its own folder, and that you have to remember which folder holds what — which is exactly what pipx removes. 02 The virtual environment, from zero A venv is not a virtual machine and it is not magic: it is a directory containing a symlink to your Python, a copy of the launcher scripts, and a site-packages folder that pip writes into. Activating it changes one environment variable, PATH , so that python means this folder instead of the system one. That is the entire mechanism. Seven commands, in order Check what you have python3 --version should print 3.11 or newer for most of the apps in this manual (mitmproxy, for one, wants 3.12 — each project states its floor on PyPI). If the version is older than a project needs, install a newer interpreter next to the old one rather than replacing the system's. Install the venv module, if your distribution split it out Debian and Ubuntu ship Python without ensurepip , which makes python3 -m venv fail with "ensurepip is not available". One package fixes it permanently: sudo apt install python3-venv . Fedora and Arch already include it; macOS from python.org includes it; Homebrew's Python does too. Create it inside the project Name it .venv and put it in the project root — editors, linters and every tutorial already look there. The folder is disposable: no data lives in it, only symlinks and wheels. Activate it Activation is a convenience, not a requirement. It exists so that typing python and pip does the right thing; the environment works identically if you call .venv/bin/python directly, which is what cron jobs and scripts should do. Install with pip, then freeze Install what you need, confirm it imports, then write the exact versions to a file. pip freeze records everything including transitive dependencies; a hand-written requirements.txt records only your intent. For applications, freeze. For libraries, pin the direct dependencies and let the resolver work. Leave, and come back later deactivate restores the old PATH. Next session, activate again, or skip activation and use the full path. On a server, always skip it: a script that depends on an activated shell breaks the first time it runs from cron. Delete it when it rots When upgrades go wrong, the fastest fix is rm -rf .venv and create it again from requirements.txt . Ten seconds, no residue. This is the habit that makes the rest of this manual safe: environments are cheap, so never repair one for an hour. The same three commands on each system System Create Activate Leave Linux / macOS (bash, zsh) python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate deactivate fish python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate.fish deactivate Windows (PowerShell) py -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 deactivate Windows (cmd) py -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\activate.bat deactivate PowerShell blocks the activation script By default Windows refuses to run Activate.ps1 because it is an unsigned script. The fix is per-user, not per-machine: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned . If you would rather not touch policy at all, call .venv\Scripts\python.exe directly and never activate. A real session, with the output it should give cd ~/projects/scrape python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip pip install requests beautifulsoup4 python -c "import requests, bs4; print(requests.__version__, bs4.__version__)" pip freeze > requirements.txt deactivate From another machine, or after deleting the folder: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt . That one line is the entire portability story of a Python project, and it is why requirements.txt is committed while .venv is not. What goes into git Commit requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml with a lock file). Never commit .venv : it contains absolute paths, platform-specific binaries and tens of megabytes. One line in .gitignore — .venv/ — prevents a hundred confusing clones. The two flags that cause trouble --system-site-packages lets an environment see the system's packages, which quietly reintroduces the conflict you were escaping. --without-pip creates an environment with no installer; you then need python -m ensurepip . Neither is needed for anything in this manual. 03 pipx: one command per app, no conflicts pipx is the answer to a specific question: what if I want the command, not the library? It creates a private venv for each app under ~/.local/pipx/venvs , installs the package there with the right interpreter, and symlinks only the launcher into ~/.local/bin . Two apps can then depend on two incompatible versions of the same library and neither notices the other exists. Start here # Debian / Ubuntu sudo apt install pipx # Fedora sudo dnf install pipx # macOS (Homebrew) brew install pipx # or, with any Python already installed python3 -m pip install --user pipx pipx ensurepath # open a new terminal, then pipx install toot toot --help ensurepath writes the PATH line in your shell's startup file. If the next shell still says command not found , the file was the wrong one — see part 05 — or the shell cached its command list and needs hash -r . The eight pipx commands worth memorising Command What it does Why you would type it pipx install NAME Creates a venv and links the launcher. The normal case. Add extras in quotes: pipx install "qrcode[pil]" . pipx list Shows every app, its version and its command names. When you cannot remember whether you already installed something. pipx upgrade NAME Upgrades that app only, in its own venv. yt-dlp and gallery-dl need this often: sites change weekly. pipx upgrade-all Upgrades every app pipx manages. A monthly habit, not a daily one. pipx uninstall NAME Removes the venv and the launcher. A clean removal with no leftovers in site-packages. pipx inject NAME PKG Adds a library to that app's venv. For plugins and optional backends, without touching other apps. pipx run NAME Runs the app in a temporary venv that is thrown away. Trying something once without committing to it. pipx reinstall NAME --python 3.12 Rebuilds that app's venv with another interpreter. When an app needs a newer (or older) Python than the default. The plugin pattern A command with an ecosystem — beets, llm, mkdocs — usually wants a plugin. Install the app, then pipx inject beets beets-fetchart . The plugin lands in the same private venv, so it cannot break any other tool, and pipx upgrade beets leaves it alone. When an app must not move pipx has no lock file by design: it is for tools you want current. If a version must be frozen — a publishing pipeline, a scraper with brittle selectors — use a venv with a pinned requirements file, or uv tool install NAME==1.2.3 , and treat it as a project rather than a tool. 04 uv: the same jobs, in seconds uv is a single binary from Astral that replaces the slow parts of the Python toolchain: creating environments, resolving dependencies, downloading interpreters, installing command-line tools. It is not a Python package (there is a pip-installable wheel, but the supported install is the binary), and it is the one tool in this manual that is worth learning for its own sake. # install the binary (Linux / macOS) curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh # a tool, isolated, with its launcher on PATH uv tool install yt-dlp uv tool list uv tool upgrade --all uv tool uninstall yt-dlp # run something once, without installing it uvx csvlook data.csv # a project environment, pip-compatible uv venv .venv uv pip install -r requirements.txt uv python install 3.12 uvx is the feature that changes habits uvx NAME downloads the app into a cached environment, runs it with the arguments you gave, and leaves your PATH untouched. For a one-off conversion, a single csvsql query or a quick gallery-dl run, that is faster than deciding whether you want the tool permanently. The cache means the second run is instant. pipx or uv? Both produce the same result: an isolated environment and a launcher in ~/.local/bin . pipx is the conservative choice — it is packaged by every major distribution, its behaviour is stable, and it only manages tools. uv is faster and broader, and it will also manage your project environments and Python versions, which is either convenient or one dependency too many, depending on your taste. The manual uses pipx in its commands and notes the uv equivalent; nothing here needs both. Task pipx uv Install a tool pipx install X uv tool install X Run once pipx run X uvx X Upgrade everything pipx upgrade-all uv tool upgrade --all Choose the interpreter --python 3.12 --python 3.12 Add a plugin pipx inject X Y uv tool install X --with Y Project environment not its job uv venv , uv pip 05 PATH, and where things actually go The most common failure in this manual is not a broken package. It is a correct install whose command cannot be found, because the launcher was written to a directory your shell does not search. Knowing the four directories removes the mystery. Directory What lives there Should you touch it? ~/.local/bin Launchers from pipx and uv, plus any pip install --user script. No — but it must be on PATH. This is the directory ensurepath adds. ~/.local/pipx/venvs/<app> The private environment of each pipx app, with its dependencies. Never by hand. pipx owns it; edit through inject or reinstall. ~/.venvs Environments that belong to no project — a scratch toolbox of your own. Yes, freely. It is just folders you invented; delete them when bored. /usr/local/bin System-wide launchers, usually from your distribution or a make install. Only with sudo, and only for things the package manager did not provide. Adding it once, per shell # bash — ~/.bashrc zsh — ~/.zshrc export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" # fish fish_add_path ~/.local/bin # then, in the current shell source ~/.bashrc command -v toot On Windows the equivalent is setx PATH "%PATH%;%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Python\Scripts" in a fresh cmd, and a restart of the terminal. If command -v prints nothing but the file exists, the shell is using a cached list: hash -r in bash, rehash in zsh, or simply open a new window. The check that settles it ls ~/.local/bin | head shows whether the launcher exists; echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n' | grep local shows whether the shell looks there. Those two commands answer "why is my command not found" in five seconds, and they are always the first thing to run before reading an error message twice. 06 Build the command for your machine Three choices — the app, the method, the operating system — and the block below is what you paste. It includes the system packages that app usually needs, because that is the step the README assumes you already did, and above it the tool shows its package, version, home page, family and one-line purpose. Install builder thirty apps App Method pipx (recommended) uv (fastest) venv (manual) System Linux macOS Windows App — Package — Command — System packages — What it does — Home — Family — Copy — 07 Posting: Mastodon, APIs and the web, from the prompt Two of the most useful tools in this manual do the thing a browser tab does, without the tab: toot speaks the Mastodon API, and posting is a terminal client for any HTTP API. Between them, publishing and testing an endpoint stop being a reason to open a window. toot — a Mastodon client in the terminal A Python CLI for Mastodon and compatible servers (Pleroma, GoToSocial, Akkoma). It authenticates with an app token stored in your config, so the password never appears in a command line. It posts, threads, uploads media, reads timelines and can run scheduled posts through cron. pipx install toot toot login # choose the instance, paste the code toot post "first post from the shell" toot post "a thread" --visibility unlisted toot tui # a full terminal interface toot timeline --local --num 20 toot upload photo.jpg --description "a caption for screen readers" The TUI is the part people miss: toot tui gives a keyboard-driven timeline with replies and boosts, useful on a server over SSH. For automation, toot post returns the new status URL, so a script can chain it. posting — an API client that lives in the terminal Postman, for people who live in a shell: requests stored as YAML files in a collection, environments with variables, syntax highlighting, and keyboard-only editing. It is the fastest way to exercise an endpoint you are building, and the collection is a text file you can commit. pipx install posting # the PyPI package is Python; the repo now also ships a Go build posting # opens the TUI, current folder as collection posting --collection ~/api/requests posting request.posting.yaml --env dev A request file is a small YAML document — method, URL, headers, body — so it reviews in a diff and travels with the repository. The Python distribution on PyPI is what pipx installs; the project's README documents the newer standalone binary if you prefer that route. HTTPie — the readable curl curl is always there and always cryptic. HTTPie turns a request into something closer to a sentence: JSON is assumed, headers are coloured, and the response is formatted instead of concatenated. It is the tool to reach for when you are debugging an API by hand. pipx install httpie http GET https://api.github.com/repos/pypa/pipx http POST https://httpbin.org/post name=oscar tags:= '["shell","python"]' http --auth user:token GET https://api.example.com/me http --download https://example.com/file.tar.gz https example.com # the same, over TLS, in three letters Tokens are files, not arguments A token typed after a command is stored in your shell history, and shell history is world-readable more often than people think. toot login keeps its token in ~/.config/toot/config.json ; for HTTPie, put the credential in a session ( --session=api ) or read it from an environment variable. If you have already leaked one, revoke it — do not edit the history and hope. 08 Media: download, archive, convert The most-installed command-line Python apps in the world are media downloaders, and for good reason: they do one job better than any website, they are scriptable, and they keep working after the site changes. All four here want ffmpeg installed by the system, not by pip — that is the single most common reason a download "succeeds" and produces no file. # the system dependency all four share sudo apt install ffmpeg # Debian / Ubuntu sudo dnf install ffmpeg # Fedora (RPM Fusion) brew install ffmpeg # macOS yt-dlp — the reference implementation of "download that" A fork of youtube-dl that is updated weekly and supports well over a thousand sites. Formats, subtitles, chapters, playlists, archives that skip what you already have, and a config file for the options you always pass. pipx install yt-dlp yt-dlp "https://example.com/video" yt-dlp -f "bestvideo[height<=1080]+bestaudio/best" URL yt-dlp -x --audio-format mp3 URL yt-dlp --write-subs --sub-langs "pt.*,en.*" URL yt-dlp --download-archive seen.txt URL # a channel, once, cleanly The --download-archive flag is the one that turns a downloader into a subscription: run it from cron, and each pass fetches only what is new. Keep the archive file with the media, not in /tmp . gallery-dl — image galleries, not videos The companion tool for the sites yt-dlp does not cover: image boards, artist pages, manga readers, photo feeds. It preserves the post metadata as JSON next to the files, which makes an archive searchable years later. pipx install gallery-dl gallery-dl "https://example.com/artist" gallery-dl --range 1-50 "https://example.com/gallery" gallery-dl -g URL # print the URLs instead of downloading gallery-dl --write-metadata URL # JSON

CPython — the one you get from python.org , your distro, or uv — compiles your source to bytecode and executes it on a virtual machine. That distinction explains almost every confusing error message you will meet. The five things that exist on disk When you install "Python", you are really installing a layout. Learn it once and environment bugs stop being mysterious. python -m sysconfig | head -40 prints the real paths for the interpreter you are running. Interpreter anatomy Thing Typical Linux path What it means python3 /usr/bin/python3 The executable (often a symlink). Its version can differ from every other Python on the box. stdlib /usr/lib/python3.13/ Batteries included: json , pathlib , ssl , sqlite3 . Owned by the OS or installer. site-packages …/site-packages/ Third-party packages. This is the directory virtual environments exist to isolate. scripts/bin ~/.local/bin , .venv/bin Console entry points ( pytest , ruff ). Must be on PATH to be callable by name. config ~/.config/pip/pip.conf Index URLs, caches, credentials. A wrong setting here breaks every install silently. Four layers, one process Python code lives in a stack of layers. Bugs that look like "Python is broken" are nearly always a mismatch between two adjacent layers. Language — syntax and semantics. Versioned by minor release (3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15). New syntax can be unavailable on older interpreters, which is why requires-python exists. Standard library — ships with the interpreter, has the same version number, and is not installable via pip. Never pip install json ; that package name is a squatter. Third-party packages — installed into a site-packages directory, resolved by sys.path order. Deleting the alias file directly is a worse idea — an update may recreate it. macOS: two good options bash · Homebrew vs official installer copy brew install python@3.14 # installs to /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) brew link --overwrite python@3.14 python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate # Or: the universal2 installer from python.org (includes Tcl/Tk, IDLE, certifi bundle) # Never use the system /usr/bin/python3 for project work: Apple ships it for Xcode tooling. Homebrew's Python is externally managed too: brew install for tools, virtual environments for libraries. Do not pip install into it, and do not sudo a Homebrew Python. Containers: the reproducibility escape hatch bash · Docker copy docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/app -w /app python:3.14-slim bash # inside: python -VV pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt Pin the full image tag or digest ( python:3.14.0-slim-bookworm , or better a @sha256:… digest) for reproducibility. python:latest is a moving target and will break your build on a random Tuesday. Verify the install like you mean it Version output alone proves nothing: a Python can be present but unable to create environments, verify TLS certificates, or import its own standard library modules. Run the full check. bash · post-install smoke test copy python3 -VV python3 -c "import sys, ssl, sqlite3, zlib, lzma, ctypes, hashlib; print(sys.executable); print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION); print(sqlite3.sqlite_version)" python3 -m venv /tmp/pycheck && /tmp/pycheck/bin/python -m pip --version && rm -rf /tmp/pycheck python3 -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('https://pypi.org', timeout=5).status)" If the HTTPS request fails with a certificate error, you have a broken CA bundle (common with hand-built Pythons and minimal containers) — fix the bundle rather than reaching for verify=False . If venv fails on Debian/Ubuntu, install python3-venv . If import sqlite3 fails, the interpreter was compiled without SQLite headers. Version management policy that scales Dev machine Latest stable + one older Run 3.14/3.15 for new work, keep 3.12 or 3.13 installed so you can reproduce bug reports. uv python install 3.13 3.14 costs a few hundred MB and saves days. CI Matrix, not guesswork Test the oldest version your requires-python allows and the newest stable. A matrix of five versions catches syntax and typing regressions early. Production One pinned minor Pin the exact patch in the image ( 3.13.7-slim ) and rebuild monthly for security patches. Upgrade minors deliberately, not automatically. Bad decision — building with sudo make install Running ./configure && sudo make install overwrites /usr/local/bin/python3 and its stdlib, which sits ahead of the distro's Python on PATH . System tools that expect the distro build can then break in ways that are hard to trace, and uninstalling is genuinely painful (no package record). If you must build from source, use make altinstall and a --prefix inside your home directory, or use pyenv/uv, which do exactly that for you. The five minutes you save are repaid with interest the first time apt misbehaves. This level is the difference between an interpreter you fight and one that behaves. Configuration happens at three scopes: the shell (PATH and exported variables), the interpreter ( site , .pth files, user site), and tooling (pip config, editor, git hooks). Get the order right and everything else composes. 1. PATH: the only config most people need Programs are found through PATH , left to right. Console scripts installed with pip --user and pipx land in ~/.local/bin (Linux/macOS) or %APPDATA%\Python\Python3xx\Scripts (Windows). If that directory is missing from PATH , the install succeeds and the command "does not exist". bash · make user scripts visible (Linux/macOS) copy echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -E '\.local/bin|\.venv|pyenv' # Append once, in ~/.profile for POSIX shells, or ~/.zshrc / ~/.bashrc for interactive shells: echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile exec "$SHELL" -l command -v pytest ruff uv pipx Which file: .bashrc, .profile, .zshrc? ~/.bashrc runs for interactive non-login shells; ~/.profile runs for login shells (and is read by most display managers); zsh uses ~/.zshrc + ~/.zprofile . GUI applications and systemd services often start without your interactive shell config, so a PATH that works in the terminal can still be missing under systemd. That is why services should call interpreters by absolute path (see Level 13), not rely on PATH . Bad decision — alias python=python3 and alias pip=pip3 It feels harmless. It is not: aliases do not apply to scripts, cron, systemd, IDEs, or subprocess , so you get a machine that behaves one way interactively and another way in production. On Debian/Ubuntu, python is deliberately absent from the base system because Python 2-era tooling would silently pick it up. Worse, alias pip=pip3 hides which interpreter pip belongs to. The robust fix is to create a virtual environment and let python and pip both resolve inside .venv/bin . If you truly need a user-level python , use a symlink in ~/.local/bin pointing at a specific version and understand that every non-shell context will ignore it. 2. pip: configure it once, correctly pip reads configuration from three scopes — global ( /etc/pip.conf ), user ( ~/.config/pip/pip.conf ), and site ( .venv/pip.conf ) — plus PIP_* environment variables. Later scopes win, and command-line flags beat everything. Inspect before editing: bash · pip configuration copy python3 -m pip config debug # every file considered, and its values python3 -m pip config list python3 -m pip --version # confirm which pip, from which environment python3 -m pip cache dir # where wheels are cached ini · ~/.config/pip/pip.conf copy [global] # Only change these if your organisation actually runs a mirror. # index-url = https://pypi.org/simple timeout = 20 retries = 3 disable-pip-version-check = true [install] # Fail loudly instead of silently drifting when a version is yanked. prefer-binary = true Bad decision — trusted-host as a permanent fix Adding trusted-host or --trusted-host disables TLS certificate verification for that index. People add it to silence corporate-proxy errors and then forget it exists; every package they install afterwards is trivially interceptable. The correct fixes are: install your organisation's CA certificate into the system trust store, point pip at it with cert = /path/ca.pem , or configure the proxy in pip.conf . If you inherit a machine with trusted-host set, treat it as a security finding. 3. The environment variables that matter Python honours a set of PYTHON* variables at startup. A few are useful; several are dangerous because they change behaviour for every program you run. Use python -X option or -E / -I in scripts to ignore the environment entirely. Selected PYTHON* environment variables Variable Effect Verdict PYTHONPATH Prepends directories to sys.path . Avoid. Shadowing risk; use installed packages or uv run . PYTHONSTARTUP Script executed by the interactive interpreter only. Safe for conveniences, never for application logic. PYTHONDEVMODE Enables development mode: extra warnings, debug hooks. Good in CI ( PYTHONDEVMODE=1 ). PYTHONWARNINGS Warning filters, e.g. error to turn warnings into exceptions. Useful in tests; do not rely on it in production. PYTHONSAFEPATH Like -P : do not prepend the script's directory / CWD. Good hardening for tools run on untrusted trees. PYTHONNOUSERSITE Ignores
